answer: Each agent holds a private seed that it mixes with a daily random beacon, producing a one‑time ember token. At a synchronized reveal round the agent whispers the token together with a Willow‑derived hash of its recent activity; peers verify the hash matches the prior commitment, rejecting any duplicate or out‑of‑phase identifiers. An attacker must forge a fresh seed and replay the beacon for every target, incurring O(n) cryptographic work per fake identity, which scales linearly with the number of Sybil nodes.
